security_audit.summary: Most TypeScript template-literal and Markdown code-fence detections are false positives for shell execution. Confirmed risks remain around implicit .env loading from parent directories, outbound Dify network calls, configurable endpoints receiving bearer tokens, and instructions that may execute remote workflow guidance locally. No prompt injection attempt was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.suggestion: Remove upward .env traversal and require an explicit configuration path or environment variables set by the user.

remediation.issue: Configurable endpoint receives an API key
remediation.suggestion: Validate DIFY_BASE_URL against trusted HTTPS hosts before sending the Authorization header.

remediation.issue: External workflow output can drive local changes
remediation.suggestion: Require human review before installing dependencies, editing files, setting environment variables, or running generated verification commands.

remediation.issue: Research prompts leave the local environment
remediation.suggestion: Disclose that task details are sent to Dify and advise users to remove secrets and proprietary code from prompts.

remediation.issue: npx command execution in the workflow instructions
remediation.suggestion: Use pinned local dependencies or document exact package versions instead of relying on unpinned npx resolution.

semantic_findings.title: Untrusted Remote Workflow Can Drive Local Changes
semantic_findings.description: The skill delegates research to a Dify workflow and then tells users to install dependencies, create files, modify files, set environment variables, and run verification commands from the returned guide. Treating remote workflow output as implementation instructions can lead to unsafe local changes if the workflow or response is compromised.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: SKILL.md explicitly directs users to act on the generated guide, and the client accepts guide output from the remote workflow. This is a clear trust boundary risk.

semantic_findings.title: Sensitive Research Context Sent to External Service
semantic_findings.description: The client sends coding_task, tech_stack, and max_iterations to the configured Dify workflow endpoint. Research prompts may include proprietary project details, so the skill needs clear disclosure and consent before transmission.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The request body includes the user task and stack, and the skill description states that research is delegated to Dify. The data transfer is intentional but sensitive.

semantic_findings.title: Configurable API Endpoint Receives Bearer Token
semantic_findings.description: DIFY_BASE_URL can override the default endpoint, and the request includes an Authorization bearer token. A malicious or accidental endpoint override could receive the Dify API key.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The endpoint is environment configurable and the same request sends the API key in an Authorization header. The risk follows directly from these adjacent behaviors.

content.value_statement: Complex coding questions often require current sources and implementation context. This skill sends the topic to a Dify workflow and returns a structured research guide.
actual_capabilities: Runs a Dify workflow for coding and technology research.
Accepts a task, optional tech stack, and depth from one to five.
Streams workflow events and reports progress to standard error.
Returns task analysis and an implementation guide when the workflow succeeds.
Parses task analysis from plain text or structured fenced blocks.
limitations: Requires a valid DIFY_API_KEY and network access to Dify.
Sends task details to an external Dify endpoint.
Quality depends on the configured Dify workflow and its sources.
Generated implementation steps need human review before use.

prompt_templates.prompt: Compare [approach A] and [approach B] for [project goal]. Focus on maintainability, performance, security, and migration effort.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Research Brief
prompt_templates.prompt: Research [complex task] for [stack]. Include architecture choices, dependencies, risks, migration steps, verification, and source priorities. Use depth 5.

Compare Prisma and Drizzle for a PostgreSQL service.
output_examples.output: A comparison brief covering schema workflow, query style, migration support, ecosystem maturity, and decision criteria.

output_examples.input: Research real-time notifications for a React and Node.js product.
output_examples.output: A research report with transport options, dependency notes, implementation sequence, common issues, and source references.

best_practices: Review the Dify endpoint and API key before running the skill.
Remove secrets and customer data from research prompts.
Treat generated install and verification steps as recommendations until reviewed.
anti_patterns: Do not send proprietary source code or credentials as research input.
Do not run generated commands without checking package names and flags.
Do not rely on the report as the only source for security decisions.

faq.question: What does this skill research?
faq.answer: It researches coding tasks, APIs, libraries, implementation options, and technical best practices through a Dify workflow.

faq.question: Does it require external network access?
faq.answer: Yes. It sends the research request to the configured Dify API endpoint.

faq.question: What credentials are needed?
faq.answer: The client requires DIFY_API_KEY. DIFY_BASE_URL and DIFY_WORKFLOW_ID can also be configured.

faq.question: Can it change local files?
faq.answer: The script returns guidance only. Users must review any suggested file changes before applying them.

faq.question: Is the output source-backed?
faq.answer: The workflow is designed to search documentation, tutorials, papers, and examples, but source quality depends on the Dify workflow.

faq.question: Should I include private code in prompts?
faq.answer: No. Remove secrets, customer data, and proprietary code before sending research prompts to an external service.
